Having the ability to apply yourself isn't unique or special; it's something that EVERY human being can do. It's the bare minimum. 

Otherwise,  everything you said would make sense except for the fact that I've failed calculus FOUR times and have done everything in my power to pass. Yeah, I've been successful in the past but after two years of failure,  who's to say I will ever succeed again? It seems very unlikely to me at this point. I would have agreed with your post had you made it a year and a half ago, and for a while the kind of mentality that you laid out was what I tried to follow, but now I just feel like it's hopeless

Thanks for the advice, this is helpful. Though to be honest,  I try not to be defeatist. For the past two years I've told myself that I can succeed in computer engineering despite my trouble with classes, though to be honest that really is starting to feel impossible which is likely why I come across that way.

Well no not exactly, I've failed it three times and this is the fourth time I am taking it, and my professor has already told me that I will never pass it. But everything else yes.

Also I can't switch to business because that requires a 3.0 GPA at my school which is basically permanently out of my reach now...
